name: B cell class switching
summary: A naive B cell (IgM, IgD) needs T cell help, CD40L binding its CD40, to switch class; the cytokines around it pick the class: IFN-γ (Th1) → IgG, IL-4 and IL-13 (Th2) → IgE, TGF-β and IL-5 → IgA. Every switch needs AID (activation-induced cytidine deaminase), which also drives affinity maturation. Hyper-IgM syndromes: CD40L (X-linked, most common), CD40, or AID defects.
tissue: germinal centers of lymph nodes, spleen and Peyer patches (IgA)

naive.name: Naive B cell (IgM, IgD)
naive.notes: Makes IgM and IgD (the same antigen-binding part, by alternative splicing). Its receptor binds antigen; it then needs T cell help to switch.

act.name: Activated B cell
aliases: B cell with T cell help
act.notes: In the germinal center: somatic hypermutation (affinity maturation) and class switching, both by AID; then plasma cells and memory B cells.

igg.name: IgG
igg.notes: The most abundant antibody and the main secondary response: crosses the placenta (FcRn), opsonizes, fixes complement, neutralizes toxins and viruses.

ige.name: IgE
ige.notes: Lowest in serum; binds mast cells and basophils (FcεRI): type I hypersensitivity, and with eosinophils against helminths. Omalizumab binds it.

iga.name: IgA
iga.notes: Mucosal antibody: crosses epithelium as a dimer (J chain) with secretory component; in breast milk. Made more than any other antibody. Selective IgA deficiency (most common immunodeficiency): sinopulmonary and GI infections, anaphylaxis to IgA in blood products.

cd40l.name: CD40L (from helper T cells)
cd40l.notes: CD40L on an activated helper T cell binds CD40 on the B cell. X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome: CD40L defect, so no class switching: high IgM, low IgG, IgA, IgE; Pneumocystis and other opportunistic infections.

sw_g.name: IFN-γ (Th1)
sw_g.notes: IFN-γ from Th1 cells favors opsonizing, complement-fixing IgG (IL-4 and IL-21 also drive IgG subclasses).
